title: Is Braze a Brazen Purchase?
excerpt: Braze sits behind a merchant's app and website, watches what a customer does and decides the next message to send.
aeo_summary: Braze sits behind a merchant's app and website, watches what a customer does and decides the next message to send. A shopper opens the merchant's app, adds a jacket to the cart and leaves. Braze sees that event as it happens and decides what to send and when.
content:
Braze sits behind a merchant's app and website, watches what a customer does and decides the next message to send. A shopper opens the merchant's app, adds a jacket to the cart and leaves. Braze sees that event as it happens and decides what to send and when.

In this issue

  • Why the Brazen Purchase and where does it fit? Marketing Cloud is the brand for the whole marketing suite, and the Marketing Cloud page names Marketing Cloud Next as the flagship, "built natively on the Salesforce platform with AI, Data 360, and Agentforce at its core."
  • Let's Talk Commerce suite. No, this is not a shameless plug for my wildly popular Talk Commerce Podcast, but I did have the pleasure of sitting down with Gordon Evans, the CMO of Commerce Cloud, at Shoptalk Nashville.
  • Who else sells what Braze sells. Adobe sells the same four pieces, commerce, content, data and engagement, under Experience Cloud.
  • Why not just use Shopify? Shopify says it can do what Salesforce does for a lot less.
  • Where the deal leaves merchants. Three kinds of merchants gain from the deal.
  • The numbers. Braze is a growing business. Revenue for the fiscal year that ended January 31 was $738.2 million, up 24.4%, and in September Braze raised its guidance for fiscal 2027 to $910 to $913 million.
